fact: Rashid 1 rover mass was about 10 kg.
source_title: Lunar mission: how Rashid rover will explore the Moon in 14 Earth days (Khaleej Times)
notes: Same 10 kg figure in EGU21 abstract and The National feature

fact: Rashid 1 had four wheels; wheels designed to climb slopes up to 20 degrees and rocks up to 10 cm high.
source_title: The Rashid rover: to guide the way for the next generation lunar missions (EGU21-14732, Almaeeni, Els, Almarzooqi, MBRSC)
notes: Official-author conference abstract; design intent, never flown

fact: Rashid 1 instruments: two wide-field navigation cameras, a microscopic imager and a thermal imager (Langmuir probe also listed by a secondary source).
source_title: Orbit Codex: Rashid (Hakuto-R)
notes: Cameras confirmed by Khaleej Times 2021; Langmuir probe only from secondary page, not independently confirmed. Same page gives 0.5x0.5x0.7 m and 10 cm/s top speed - single secondary source, not recorded as verified

fact: A UAE wheel-terrain paper gives the Rashid wheel as 0.1 m diameter, 7.5 mm wide, 12 fixed grousers 10 mm high, wheel weight 1 kg.
source_title: Advance Simulation Method for Wheel-Terrain Interactions of Space Rovers: A Case Study on the UAE Rashid Rover (Abubakar, Alhammadi, Zweiri, Seneviratne; Khalifa University KUCARS)
notes: Partly supported by MBRSC per paper. Preprint; peer-review status not checked

fact: The same paper modelled soil with a modified Reece pressure-sinkage model plus Wong shear model, using an MBRSC regolith sample representing Lacus Somniorum; simulator was Vortex Studio.
source_title: Advance Simulation Method ... Rashid Rover (arXiv 2308.12431)
notes: Lunar regolith, not dune sand. Tuned params include n 1->1.1 and phi 28->23 deg

fact: Single-wheel rig results at slip 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75: experimental sinkage 0.010, 0.0158, 0.0169, 0.0192 m; drawbar pull 5.2, 10.1, 16.77, 24.1 N.
source_title: Advance Simulation Method ... Rashid Rover (arXiv 2308.12431)
notes: Same data used for tuning and validation (not independent); no error metric given; slip tested only to 0.75; lunar simulant. Useful as a UAE-origin slip/sinkage data point on a rigid grousered wheel

fact: Khalifa University master's thesis (2022, Mariam Alhammadi) analysed Rashid-1 wheels with terramechanics and FEA; reports peak tractive efficiency at 10-15% slip and that larger grousers raise drawbar pull while generally reducing sinkage.
source_title: Lunar Rover Wheels Design & Analysis (Khalifa University Khazna)
notes: Thesis full text not read; only abstract

fact: A 2022 IAC paper (Alhammadi et al.) used finite element analysis on Rashid wheel and grouser geometry on lunar regolith; beyond a point larger diameter, more or taller grousers do not further reduce required drawbar pull.
source_title: Finite Element Simulations of the Wheels of the Rashid Lunar Rover (IAC 2022, Paris)
notes: Abstract only

fact: Samples from ESA, CREST (Universite libre de Bruxelles), Cambridge Graphene Centre, York University and others were bonded to Rashid 1's wheels for a Material Adhesion and Abrasion Detection experiment.
source_title: Samples on rover wheels (ESA Multimedia)
notes: Dust/adhesion topic: only noted as wheel context; thermal/dust effects left to sibling repo hudasol/dhill

fact: Rashid 1 was carried by ispace's Hakuto-R Mission 1 lander, which failed to land on 2023-04-26 (JST); the rover never reached the surface.
source_title: ispace press release (results of Mission 1 lunar landing)
notes: Fetched summary did not confirm the rover was named on the ispace page; rover-aboard fact comes from Gulf News and Khaleej Times (other rows). Date conflict: 26 Apr JST vs 25 Apr UTC reported by other sources (1:43 JST = 16:43 UTC 25 Apr)

fact: ispace attributed the failure to software: the altitude sensor reading over a crater rim was discarded, so the lander believed it was at zero altitude when about 5 km up and ran out of propellant.
source_title: ispace press release (Mission 1 results)
notes: Orbit Codex gives a similar account (secondary)

fact: Rashid 1 landing target was Atlas crater (47.5N, 44.4E) on the southeastern edge of Mare Frigoris; UAE planned to change the site for the second rover.
source_title: Revealed: UAE to alter landing site on Moon for second lunar rover ... (Gulf News)
notes: Gulf News also says samples on the wheels would continue and mobility, comms and systems would be improved; plans as of Feb 2024

fact: MBRSC's Director General said in May 2023 the team had not yet decided any technical improvements for the next rover, because Rashid 1 never operated on the Moon.
source_title: Exclusive: UAE will achieve its Moon landing dream with Rashid Rover 2 (Khaleej Times)
notes: Superseded in part by the Feb 2024 Gulf News statement of intent to improve mobility; no wheel design for Rashid 2 found

fact: Rashid 2 will fly on Firefly Aerospace's Blue Ghost Mission 2 to the Moon's far side; Firefly said the rover will test various wheel materials for durability in lunar dust.
source_title: Firefly Aerospace Adds UAE's Rashid 2 Rover to Blue Ghost Mission (Firefly)
notes: Mass and wheel count not stated on page. Dust durability: cross-ref only, see dhill

fact: MBRSC completed Rashid 2 and shipped it to the US for preparation with Firefly; funded by the TDRA ICT Fund.
source_title: MBRSC completes development of Rashid Rover 2 (BroadcastPro ME)
notes: Mass, wheels, mobility changes not mentioned. Source is trade press relaying MBRSC

fact: Rashid 2 testing included drive-off and deployment trials with Firefly in the US, antenna/arm deployment under simulated lunar gravity and vibration tests at EARTH (an EDGE subsidiary) in the UAE, and thermal-vacuum testing at CNES Toulouse.
source_title: UAE to the Moon: New milestone for Rashid Rover 2 (Gulf News)
notes: No wheel or traction test results given; Khaleej Times 2025-12-11 confirms drive-off simulations

fact: Hope carries three instruments: a colour imager, infrared spectrometer and ultraviolet spectrometer, studying atmosphere and escape; no surface mobility role.
